source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to continue autonomous LeanFrontier formalization and delegated target selection. Live-state auditing showed that the finite weighted, finite-PMF, and arbitrary-probability-space Paley-Zygmund inequalities had merged, as had Cantelli's inequality, while Mathlib and LeanFrontier searches found no Chung-Erdos or Kochen-Stone inequality. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the finite-event Chung-Erdos inequality as a substantive consumer of the accepted measure-theoretic Paley-Zygmund theorem and as a natural stepping stone toward Kochen-Stone/Borel-Cantelli developments. The proof defines the finite event-count random variable X = sum_i 1_{A_i}, proves its first moment is sum_i P(A_i), its second moment is sum_{i,j} P(A_i intersect A_j), identifies {X > 0} with the union of the events, and applies the accepted Paley-Zygmund theorem at theta = 0. The formal Lean statement and proof were authored by GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT; the human did not author or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
